clue.text: Game controller's pleasures facing credit

indicators.note: facing here just sets one piece up against the next, in order

parts.note: joys are pleasures or delights
buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: A gamer's delights are set against a credit line.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK is informal British for credit, as in buying 'on tick'. The 's of 'controller's' reads as 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the hand-held lever used to steer play in video games.

clue.text: Determined to support black high fliers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: Someone resolute props up a group of dark-clad high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' places SET under JET in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy socialites who travel the world, figuratively flying high.

clue.text: American pulled for the most part with energy

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: yanked means pulled sharply
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A US citizen gave a hard tug, mostly with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts the D from YANKED, leaving YANKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is a common informal term for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Try smack

explanation.surface: An order to sample a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: To try food is to sample its flavour; a smack is a slight flavour or trace, as in 'a smack of garlic'.

clue.text: City will give encouragement to ring road

indicators.note: ring means encircle, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: A town's supporters will ring the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is the container signal, though it doubles as part of the ring road picture. Chester is a historic walled city in north-west England; 'will give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is an English cathedral city in Cheshire.

clue.text: Half of them run, suffering from excitement

indicators.note: the first half of the word them is taken, two of its four letters

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
ill means sick or suffering

explanation.surface: Half the group make a dash while unwell, from sheer excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes TH from 'them'; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden surge of excitement or pleasure.

clue.text: A penance that's a shock — right this wrong!

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

indicators.note: wrong means put out of its proper arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something shocking needs putting right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges R and THIS into SHIRT. 'shock' looks like a surprise but is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough garment worn next to the skin as self-punishment, so a form of penance.

clue.text: Play it, and men get together

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are toyed with and moved about

explanation.surface: Act it, and the men gather as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' rearranges ITANDMEN; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means working jointly, side by side.

clue.text: Rigging lines from patios to support plant centre

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath
the centre of plant is its middle three letters

parts.note: yards are paved outdoor areas like patios

explanation.surface: Ropes are taken from terraces to hold up a central plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes LAN from 'plant'; 'to support' sets YARDS beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanyards are short cords used on ships to secure or tighten rigging.

clue.text: Element found speaking languages between 9 and 11

indicators.note: speaking signals we go by how the word is pronounced

parts.note: tongues are languages, as in speaking in tongues
the number between nine and eleven is ten

explanation.surface: A chemical element is discovered in a multilingual setting between two numbered points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' says TUNGS as the word for languages; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is the metallic chemical element W, used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: Pay attention to opponents chasing schedule

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows

parts.note: a list is a schedule or roster
E and N, East and North, are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Heed the rival team as they race after the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and North sit as rivals, so 'opponents' can give EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to heed or attend to what is said.

clue.text: Student found in bed — idiot!

indicators.note: found in signals one piece sitting inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L for learner is a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner discovered asleep, and called a fool for it.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates British student drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Rambling tale about the French soldiers with spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the rest
rambling means wandering, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the four letters of tale are taken to be rearranged
le is French for the
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A meandering story concerning French troops and their spirited exploits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' makes ETAL, and 'about' wraps it round the inner pieces. ELEMENTAL is used as a noun here, so 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a nature spirit of earth, air, fire or water in folklore.

clue.text: None, oddly, found in water plant

indicators.note: found in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: the sea is a body of water

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Not a single one turns up in an aquatic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water plant' looks like one phrase, but 'water' gives its own piece and 'plant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a cassia shrub whose leaves give a laxative.

clue.text: Reported to be hurting fly

indicators.note: reported means as heard, by pronunciation

parts.note: sore means hurting or aching

explanation.surface: An insect is said to be painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; 'fly' looks like the insect but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to fly high in the air.

clue.text: Managing director is lost at sea

parts.note: to be over something is to manage it, in charge of it
a director sits on the board, the governing body standing in for its member

explanation.surface: A company boss has vanished on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A managing director is in charge of, or over, the board; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown or fallen over the ship's side is gone into the water.

clue.text: The last few dealt in transport

indicators.note: transport means carry off, so the letters are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: The remaining few were traded through shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' rearranges DEALTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the final part, the few remaining at the end.

clue.text: Beer drinking job on Sunday for the preachers

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so this comes last
drinking means taking in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Clergy enjoy a pint after their Sunday work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' splits the beer around the job, and 'on' in a down clue sets Sunday's letter below. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the twelve disciples sent out to spread Christ's teaching.

clue.text: Aunt Sally

parts.note: a fairground throwing game, and also a figure set up to be attacked or criticised

explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a target of easy criticism, someone open to attack, and literally a game played at fairs.

clue.text: People who fork out to accept trainee actors

indicators.note: accept means take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: payers are people who fork out money
L stands for learner, a trainee

explanation.surface: Customers paying up welcome trainee performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts L inside PAYERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Players are performers on stage, as in a troupe of travelling players.

clue.text: Bag a drink from Spain

explanation.surface: Pick up a Spanish beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a large bag; sack was also an old name for sherry, a fortified wine from Spain.

clue.text: Mine has hard centre

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A mine with a tough core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the essential core or heart of something.

clue.text: Left ten out as a warning

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten were left out, taken as an ill omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen or sign of something coming.

clue.text: Father and I hear a comic character

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: hear signals the letter is said aloud and spelt as its sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: A dad says he hears a funny figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' turns I into its sound-alike EYE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating sailor of cartoon strips.

clue.text: Watch nurse have a go

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: A carer tries keeping a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a guard posted on watch.

clue.text: Operators do it before cutting vegetation

explanation.surface: Surgeons wash before they cut into the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash thoroughly before operating; scrub is also low stunted bushland.

clue.text: Playing once — or it's hormone treatment

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with and reordered

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as they stand, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Performing at once, or it's down to steroid injections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges ONCE plus ORITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortisone is a steroid hormone given to reduce inflammation.

clue.text: Country home needs to raise help

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A nation's household must collect aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns AID upward to DIA; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia.

clue.text: Animals that are little backed circle area

indicators.note: circle means go round, so one piece surrounds the other
backed means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: small means little

explanation.surface: Beasts that are small reversed round a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SMALL into LLAMS, and 'circle' puts it round A: LLAM-A-S. 'that are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids kept as pack animals.

clue.text: Democrat reacted strangely to sure-fire winner

indicators.note: strangely signals letters arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: A politician responded oddly to a racing certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Democrat's initial stays at the front, and only the verb is scrambled by 'strangely'; in racing slang a dead cert is a horse certain to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead cert is a certainty, often a horse sure to win.

clue.text: Not easily shaken by one's partner

explanation.surface: A steady sort, unshaken by a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means firm and stable; a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend.

clue.text: Plan to get back into drift

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to stray is to drift off course

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: the word get is used as written

explanation.surface: A scheme to recover lost ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TEG, which 'into' places inside the drift word; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategy is an overall plan of action.
